Your path to Ontario licensing

To become eligible for Ontario's provincial security guard licensing examination, you must complete training that meets the province's requirements through an eligible training provider, including all 12 syllabus areas or accepted existing first aid certification. The security curriculum in this portal allocates 33.5 hours of security instruction across Modules 1–11, alongside Module 12: recognized emergency first aid and CPR certification. Ontario requires at least 40 hours total including first aid, or 33.5 hours excluding first aid when valid certification is supplied.

The recognized first aid component is generally allocated 6.5 hours in Ontario’s syllabus. Delivery format and accepted hours depend on the approved first aid provider and course. Students must complete all practical skills and certification requirements; the online portion alone is not sufficient.

1. Study
Complete Modules 1–11 and their required instructional time; meet the separate Module 12 certification requirement.
2. Demonstrate learning
Complete each required scenario, achieve 100% on each matching game, and at least 95% on each internal module quiz.
3. Complete first aid
Obtain accepted emergency first aid and CPR certification, including AED training where offered.
4. Verify completion
Have the provider validate attendance, certification and training records.
5. Take provincial test
Follow Ontario's process for the provincial licensing examination.
6. Apply for licence
After meeting applicable requirements, submit your licence application.

The 95% scores are this course's internal standards, not the provincial exam pass mark. Completing this HTML demo does not itself establish provincial exam eligibility.

Why take this course?

A strong security guard does more than memorize rules. Employers need personnel who can notice hazards, prevent incidents, treat people fairly, respond calmly to emergencies, preserve evidence and write reports that other professionals can rely on.

Our learning approach connects legislation with realistic situations: handling unauthorized visitors, managing conflict, conducting patrols, assisting vulnerable people, communicating with emergency responders and making careful decisions under pressure. The goal is to help you arrive at your first assignment with a foundation in safety, professionalism and sound judgment.

Students can review lessons, listen to narrated material, read transcripts, practise scenarios and revisit any module. Instructors should remain accessible for real-time questions and guidance when the course is delivered as qualifying online training.

Where can a security licence take you?

Ontario security guards work across many environments. Each employer may require extra site-specific training, screening or qualifications.

✈️ Airport and transportation security
🏬 Shopping malls and retail security
🛍️ Loss prevention
🏢 Residential concierge and building security
🎟️ Concerts and special events
🚗 Mobile patrol and alarm response
🏥 Healthcare and institutional security
🌙 Nightclubs and licensed premises
🏗️ Construction and industrial sites
🤝 Close protection (additional training may be required)

A licence does not independently qualify someone for every specialized assignment; employer and site requirements still apply.

Course curriculum: all 12 modules

The following modules make up the Ontario security guard training syllabus. Modules 1–11 cover security instruction; Module 12 requires recognized first aid certification.

1. Introduction to the Security Industry

Roles, responsibilities, professional conduct, and the private security industry.

2. The Private Security and Investigative Services Act

Ontario’s PSISA, licensing duties, regulations, and the Ministry Code of Conduct.

3. Basic Security Procedures

Patrols, surveillance, access control, crowds, traffic, handovers, and drug effects.

4. Report Writing

Accurate notes, incident reports, evidence, and professional documentation.

5. Health and Safety

Workplace hazards, WHMIS symbols, safe practices, and worker responsibilities.

6. Emergency Response Preparation

Emergency recognition, evacuation, fire safety, and scene management.

7. Canadian Legal System

Criminal and civil law, courts, evidence, and legal proceedings.

8. Legal Authorities

Trespass, arrest powers and limits, lawful authority, and police involvement.

9. Effective Communications

Listening, radio communication, conflict resolution, and de-escalation.

10. Sensitivity Training

Human rights, accessibility, cultural awareness, and respectful service.

11. Use of Force Theory

Legal limits on force, risk assessment, avoidance, and accountability.

12. Emergency Level First Aid Certification

Recognized emergency first aid and CPR certification; external practical assessment required.

Assessment and student support

You may study the 11 online modules in any order. Each online security module has a separate study-time requirement, a required scenario, a matching game requiring 100%, and a quiz requiring at least 95%. After all required module activities are completed, the 60-question final exam unlocks. You must answer at least 57 questions correctly to achieve the course's internal 95% target.

Each module offers narrated slides and readable text. For help, use Instructor support in the course menu to configure or open the instructor's contact link.

Important: This is a browser-based demonstration. Timers and quiz records stored locally are not independently verified. A live qualifying course needs secure student identities, reliable instructional-time verification, accessible real-time instructor interaction, recognized first aid/CPR certification, provider records and compliance review.
